entries.clue: Idle talk: "Leave, piss off!" (6)

indicatorNotes.off: off as in gone off, spoilt: the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: Someone told to stop gossiping replies with a rude brush-off.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make "Leave, piss off!" look like one insult; really it is two instructions, GO and a jumbled PISS.
annotation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk about other people's business.

entries.clue: Survive being declared gay at the end (7)

annotation.surface: Someone finally comes out late in life and endures.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one story about coming out late; in fact "Survive" stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To outlast something is to survive longer than it.

entries.clue: Round pub entrance, dropped kinky belt? (5)

indicatorNotes.Round: round as a preposition means surrounding, so one piece encircles the other
indicatorNotes.entrance: the entrance of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A pub-goer drops something at the door of a bar and it turns out to be a kinky belt.
annotation.walkthrough: "Round" sits at the front, so it looks like a round of drinks; it tells you to put SANK around P. The question mark flags a belt as a blow, not a strap.
annotation.definitionFit: To belt is to hit, and a spank is the kinky version of that blow.

entries.clue: Funding McFadden and DeSantis takes time (9)

blocks.note: an age = a period of time

annotation.surface: A news line about bankrolling two politicians taking a long time.
annotation.walkthrough: Two surnames stand in for first names: Pat McFadden is a British Labour minister and Ron DeSantis a Republican governor of Florida.
annotation.definitionFit: Patronage is the financial support given by a patron.

entries.clue: One hoping for beneficial response is unable to take Liam's eruption? (8)

indicatorNotes.take: CANT takes the jumbled letters inside it
indicatorNotes.eruption: an eruption throws LIAM's letters about

annotation.surface: Someone cannot cope with another tantrum from Liam Gallagher.
annotation.walkthrough: "Beneficial response" hides benefits: a benefit claimant hopes for a payout. Liam's eruptions suggest Liam Gallagher of Oasis, famous for outbursts.
annotation.definitionFit: A benefit claimant hopes the state will respond with benefit payments.

entries.clue: Stock Conservative – pain (5)

annotation.surface: A Tory who is a stock type and a pain.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stock Conservative" reads as a stereotyped Tory, but "Stock" is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store or stock of things.

entries.clue: Summer will do, to make sense (3,2)

blocks.note: read summer as sum-mer, one who does sums: what would such a person do?
the everyday idiom for a story or excuse that holds together

annotation.surface: Some season will do if it helps things make sense.
annotation.walkthrough: "Summer" looks like the season; here it is someone who sums, and what a summer does is add up.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one phrasal verb: literally totting figures, and idiomatically an explanation that holds together.

entries.clue: I'm tired of being beaten and ashamed (9)

indicatorNotes.being beaten: beaten letters are knocked out of shape

annotation.surface: A loser complains that constant defeat is humiliating.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is a whole phrase, "I'm tired of", which reads so naturally that it is easy to miss that it has exactly nine letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, and the whole clue reads straight too: someone tired of being beaten feels humiliated.

entries.clue: Tabloid upset about cryptic clue's central part (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns SUN upside down
indicatorNotes.cryptic: cryptic means obscured, so the word's letters are disguised by rearranging them
indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of around, so the reversed paper wraps round the clue

blocks.note: The Sun, the tabloid newspaper, reversed

annotation.surface: A tabloid is annoyed about the key part of a crossword clue.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper. "Cryptic clue" reads as a fixed phrase about the puzzle itself, which hides that cryptic is telling you to jumble CLUE.
annotation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central part around which something is built.

entries.clue: Double-crossed on UK/US round trip, leaders of Al-Qaida try launching stunt (8)

indicatorNotes.leaders: the leaders of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Al-Qaida, try, launching
an antic is a prank or stunt

annotation.surface: A terror group plots an attack on a transatlantic flight.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a round trip from the UK to the US crosses the Atlantic twice, once each way.
annotation.definitionFit: Flying Britain to America and back means crossing the Atlantic Ocean twice.

entries.clue: Frank's awful, Tom's heartless (6)

blocks.note: a tom is a male CAT; without its middle A it is CT

annotation.surface: Two men compared: Frank is dreadful and Tom is cruel.
annotation.walkthrough: Frank and Tom look like two men's names. Frank is the definition, and Tom stands for the animal it names, a cat.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone frank is direct, saying plainly what they think.

entries.clue: see 24dn.
Extortionate, messy divorce overwhelms poor rep (10)

indicatorNotes.messy: messy means untidy, and an untidy word has its letters strewn out of order
indicatorNotes.overwhelms: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the jumbled DIVORCE swallows the other piece
indicatorNotes.poor: poor means in bad shape, so the letters are knocked out of their order

annotation.surface: A bitter divorce costs a fortune and ruins someone's reputation.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rep" looks like reputation, and divorce lawyers do charge a lot; both are just letters to jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs extortionately more than it is worth.

entries.clue: Free up AI? Not ideal (7)

indicatorNotes.Free: set the letters free to fall into a new order

annotation.surface: A worry that letting artificial intelligence off the leash would be a bad idea.
annotation.walkthrough: "Not" looks like it belongs to "Not ideal"; it is fodder, and "ideal" stands alone. The punctuation is there to break up the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Utopian means ideal, as in a perfect imagined society.

entries.clue: Controversial European – he's to be dismissed by Gove? (9)

indicatorNotes.to be dismissed: HE is sent out of the name

blocks.clueFragment: he's to be dismissed by Gove
blocks.note: Michael Gove's first name, MICHAEL, minus HE

annotation.surface: A divisive European politician is to be sacked by Michael Gove.
annotation.walkthrough: Michael Gove is a Conservative politician; "by Gove" points to his first name, from which HE is removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Polemical writing or argument is controversial and attacking.

entries.clue: Pisspoor parties trail (7)

indicatorNotes.Pisspoor: piss-poor means badly done, so the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: Rubbish parties that drag on.
annotation.walkthrough: "Trail" is a verb here, to trudge wearily along, not a path.
annotation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trail wearily from place to place.

entries.clue: No Brexiteer recruits duke for balance (9)

indicatorNotes.recruits: REMAINER takes D into its ranks

blocks.note: someone who voted against Brexit was a Remainer

annotation.surface: A pro-EU campaigner enlists an aristocrat to give the debate balance.
annotation.walkthrough: "Balance" is the accounting sense, what is left over, not fairness.
annotation.definitionFit: A bookkeeping synonym: the balance of a sum owed is what still remains after part is paid.

entries.clue: Nurse's hand-out prior to operational cuts? (7)

annotation.definition: Nurse's hand-out prior to operational cuts?

blocks.note: surface reading: a payment or benefit given to nurses; setter's reading: the thing a theatre nurse hands out to the surgeon
surface reading: budget cuts to operations; setter's reading: the incisions made in a surgical operation

annotation.surface: Nurses receive hand-outs before government spending cuts.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hand-out" suggests welfare and "operational cuts" budget cuts; really a theatre nurse hands the surgeon a scalpel before the incisions of an operation.
annotation.definitionFit: In surgery the nurse hands out the scalpel that makes the operation's cuts.

entries.clue: Tweet about rugby players – "get more gay!" (5,2)

indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of around, so the tweet wraps round the players

blocks.note: a bird's tweet is a cheep
RU = Rugby Union; placed inside CHEE…P

annotation.surface: A social-media post urges a rugby team to be more openly gay.
annotation.walkthrough: "Gay" is used in its older sense, cheerful.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheer up! tells someone to become more cheerful, the old sense of gay.

entries.clue: Dash from South Central General (7)

annotation.surface: A patient is rushed out of South Central General hospital.
annotation.walkthrough: "South Central General" reads as a hospital name; "Dash" is a tiny amount, as in a dash of milk, not a sprint.
annotation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a very small amount, like a dash.

entries.clue: Old lover stuck on holiday island – shit (7)

indicatorNotes.stuck on: in a down clue, one piece stuck on another sits on top of it

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
Crete, the Greek island; EX sits on top of it

annotation.surface: Someone's ex is stranded on a holiday island, and it's awful.
annotation.walkthrough: "Shit" looks like an exclamation of dismay; it is the verb. In a down clue, "stuck on" puts EX above CRETE.
annotation.definitionFit: A vulgar synonym: the crude verb and the clinical one name the same bodily function.

entries.clue: Topping liberal leader in revolting evil crime (10)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: the L goes in among the other letters
indicatorNotes.revolting: the letters are in revolt, out of order

annotation.surface: Killing a Liberal leader is a disgusting and wicked crime.
annotation.walkthrough: "Topping" looks like killing, which fits the crime; it is a cake topping. Chocolate vermicelli are sprinkles for desserts.
annotation.definitionFit: Chocolate vermicelli are thin strands sprinkled as a topping on cakes and ice cream.

entries.clue: China's main bank is to get into laundering? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: laundering is a noun; its result is money made clean

indicatorNotes.main: the main part of China here is its leading letter

blocks.note: a plane banks as it leans

annotation.surface: China's biggest bank is to get involved in money laundering.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bank" looks like the financial institution, which fits laundering; it is the verb meaning to tilt. Laundering makes dirty money clean.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose, question-marked definition by result: laundering, of clothes or of dirty money, is the process of cleaning.

entries.clue: Pal's balls' ultimately grotesque descent (5)

indicatorNotes.balls: balls as in a balls-up, a mess: the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A friend's testicles are sagging grotesquely.
annotation.walkthrough: "Balls" is the mess in a balls-up, so it tells you to jumble PALS.
annotation.definitionFit: A lapse is a descent or decline into a worse state, as in a lapse into bad habits.

entries.clue: In brief, a celeb's tackle (4)

indicatorNotes.In: the answer is in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A newspaper brief about a celebrity's genitals.
annotation.walkthrough: "In brief" looks like it means "in short", and "tackle" looks like genitals; the verb tackle, to confront, is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of confronting: you tackle or face a difficulty.

entries.clue: (& 11ac.) Scrap retreat and counter-attack (5)

blocks.note: to back off or back away is to retreat

annotation.surface: Military orders: abandon the retreat and strike back instead.
annotation.walkthrough: "Scrap" looks like an order to cancel the retreat; it is the noun, a fight. The answer continues into 11 across.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean returning an attack rather than taking it.

entries.clue: Minor service provider chain acquired by Native American people (6)

indicatorNotes.acquired by: a firm acquired by another is absorbed into it, so CH goes inside the people

blocks.note: the Cree, a Native American people
ch = chain, an old unit of length; goes inside CRE…E

annotation.walkthrough: "Minor" is a child, not small: a crèche provides childcare. CH is the abbreviation for chain, a surveyor's measure of 22 yards.
annotation.definitionFit: A crèche provides a service, day care, for minors.

entries.clue: Descent of terrible dirge into tinkle (8)

indicatorNotes.terrible: a terrible dirge has its letters mangled
indicatorNotes.into: the jumbled letters go into PEE

annotation.surface: An awful funeral song declines into a faint tinkling sound.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tinkle" suggests a bell, but it is slang for urinating. "Descent" is ancestry, not a fall.
annotation.definitionFit: Descent in the sense of ancestry, not falling: a pedigree records who descends from whom.

entries.clue: Wealth measure splits unhappy couple (8)

indicatorNotes.splits: EN splits the jumbled letters apart

blocks.note: an en is a printer's measure; it goes inside OPUL…CE

annotation.surface: Money trouble drives a wedge between an unhappy couple.
annotation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of width, half an em; crosswords use it as a stock "measure".
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the word stresses wealth on show, lavish and luxurious.

entries.clue: Rogue chops off racehorse's head (6)

indicatorNotes.chops off: to chop off is to sever with a blade, so a part of the word is cut away
indicatorNotes.head: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a horse bred for harness racing, pulling a light cart at a trot
the first letter of that horse's name, the one chopped off

annotation.surface: A villain decapitates a racehorse, as in The Godfather.
annotation.walkthrough: A trotter is a horse bred for harness racing, where it trots pulling a light cart; lose the head and the rogue remains.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotter is an old-fashioned word for a rogue or cad.
